title: Backup by dump and by snapshot, and why they are not equivalent

videos.script: There are two ways to back up MongoDB, and they produce two very different things. {{two}} A dump asks the server for every document and writes them out. Small, portable, and slow to bring back, because every index has to be built again. {{dump}} A snapshot copies the files on disk. Big, quick to restore, and only safe if the server holds still while you copy. {{snapshot}} You will take both, from the same shop, while payments are still arriving. {{writes}} You will see why a dump of a busy database needs the oplog, and why a dump of a sharded cluster has no single moment at all. {{moment}} Then the part most teams skip. You will restore the dump into a server that has never seen the shop. And you will check it, collection by collection, against the original. {{restore}} One collection will not match. That is the finding. It tells you what a restore loses, and how often your backups need to run. {{finding}}
